content: We have carbon NMR peaks. Need number of methyl (CH3) groups. Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm. In data we have peaks at 19.40 (double) and 34.50 (double) and 62.10 (double). 62 likely O-CH2. 34.5 could be CH2 or CH3 attached to something. 19.4 typical methyl. There are two peaks at 19.40 (duplicate maybe due to symmetry). That suggests one unique carbon environment for methyl, but could be two equivalent methyl groups giving same shift, appearing as one peak but intensity maybe double. However carbon NMR list includes each carbon signal, not multiplicity. If molecule has two equivalent methyls, they'd give one signal. But we need count of methyl groups, not distinct signals. Need more info. Could use proton NMR to see number of methyl protons. Let's get proton NMR.
